verdict.line: You lose if you facecheck his 950-range Q or walk into his W-into-Q combo; you win if you punish his Q cooldown windows with Q-into-E knockup before level 6.

brief.thesis: Cho'Gath's Q (Rupture, 950 range) outranges both your Q (Volcanic Rupture, 800 range) and E (Searing Charge, 450 range), so he can poke you for free whenever it's up. The matchup swings on whether you respect that 9/8.5/8/7.5/7s cooldown window or punish it — Ornn holds the lane and solo-kill edge here, but the 49% head-to-head over 192 games says that edge only shows up when you play the cooldown correctly.

theirWindow.when: his Q and W both off cooldown
theirWindow.what: OP.GG flags his W (Feral Scream, 300 range cone, silences) into Q (Rupture, 950 range, pops and slows) as the real threat combo. Stay outside 300 range unless you intend to commit, and never stand still inside his cone while his Q is also up.

yourWindow.when: right after he lands or whiffs Q
yourWindow.what: His Rupture is down for 9/8.5/8/7.5/7s with no other ranged tool until level 6. Step up, land Q (Volcanic Rupture) for the slow, then E (Searing Charge) into the magma pillar it drops for a guaranteed knockup trade.

powerCurve.note: both poking, feeling for Q range
R Forge God outscales his short-range Feast

start.why: Highest-performing start into this matchup (50% WR over 138 games, 57.7% pick) — the regen and damage reduction on hits under 3 eats the chip from his auto-attack Vorpal Spikes while you poke CS.

boots.why: 51.1% WR over 141 games, 62.7% pick. Tenacity cuts the duration of his Feral Scream silence and the slow from Rupture, both of which are what let him land Feast afterward.

core.why: First item in every listed build path — the AoE empowered auto and magic resist answer his sustained W/Q magic poke.
Follows Hollow Radiance in every core path tracked; the damage-reduction shield lets you tank Feral Scream + Rupture trades without losing the fight.
71.4% WR over the 7 games that ran this third item — the magic shield directly blunts his Q/W magic damage burst before he has true-damage Feast online.

situational.when: the enemy team stacks magic damage and you need scaling resist into the late game
he or his team leans on sustained autoattacks and crit rather than burst
he builds lifesteal or grievous wounds utility becomes necessary
he rushes early autoattack trades off Vorpal Spikes and you need the sustain rush

runes.keystoneWhy: Since his Q outranges your engage tools, you need a sustain keystone to win the forced melee trades once you do close the gap — the permanent health growth also outlasts his flat Feast true damage over a long game.

summoners.why: Flash+Teleport runs 50.3% WR at 77.9% pick — Teleport resets the wave after his longer Q range chips your CS, then lets you return with the plate push. Flash is also your out from the 175-range Feast execute.

playing.title: Hold outside his Q range
playing.detail: Rupture reaches 950 while your Q and E only reach 800 and 450. Don't push the wave into his threat range just to farm; wait for his Q to be down before stepping up.

playing.title: Trade the instant his Q is down
playing.detail: After he fires Rupture, it's gone for 9/8.5/8/7.5/7s with nothing else ranged until level 6. Step in with Q for the slow, then E through the resulting magma pillar for a guaranteed knockup.

playing.title: Respect the W-into-Q combo
playing.detail: Feral Scream (300 range cone, silences) into Rupture is the exact combo OP.GG calls out. If both are up, don't stand in his 300-range cone unless you're committing to the fight.

playing.title: Don't auto-trade into Vorpal Spikes
playing.detail: His passive adds extra damage to every auto he lands on you in melee. Before level 6, use Q's slow to disengage rather than standing in prolonged auto exchanges.

playing.title: Track Feast's 175 range
playing.detail: Feast is a 60s-cooldown true-damage execute but he has to walk adjacent to use it. Keep Flash up or hold at Q range so he can't safely land it during an all-in.

playing.title: Use your own R to answer his all-in
playing.detail: Call of the Forge God comes online at 6 with a 140/120/100/100/100s cooldown. The recast redirect can body-block or catch him mid-animation when he commits to his short-range Feast.

playing.title: Itemize into his autoattacks, not just his nuke
playing.detail: If he leans on sustained autos or lifesteal rather than burst, pivot Kaenic Rookern toward Randuin's Omen, Thornmail, or Bramble Vest from the situational pool.

brief.patchCaveat: Build paths, rune pages, summoner spells, and all win-rate/pick-rate figures above are pulled from measured OP.GG games on the current patch; the mechanical reasoning and trade-timing advice tying those numbers together is our own tactical read, not measured data.

stats.opponentTip: Be careful of Cho’Gath’s (W)-(Q) combo as it becomes difficult to dodge his (Q) if hit with (W). Use your [R] carefully considering his (Q) and (W) in mind. Manage your health well to avoid being nuked by his (R).
